column1: # Classified differences between an adapter and the references, for
# These are not bugs: each entry is a deliberate or upstream-imposed semantic
# difference, documented in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md. A failing step listed here,
# for the adapter that failed it, makes its fixture a known difference with a
# waiver in results.json instead of a failure. An entry whose step passes in a
# run with that adapter is stale and fails the run. The references (native,
# python) have no entry: they pass every case.
#   3  step index in the fixture's expectations
#   4  outcome that adapter returns (interop-probe's normalised outcome)
#   5  evidence URL (the waiver's evidence in results.json)
#   6  what differs and why (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md has the details)

column6: intentional: item code 0x03 for a write to an existing, read-only DB (Siemens 03H "object access is not allowed"); both references send 0x0A because Snap7 maps every refused write to it (otfabric/snap7-interop#19)
